chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskān, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Perform ghusl on the day of al-Aḍḥā, al-Fiṭr, and Friday, and when you have washed a dead person. But do not perform ghusl from touching him when you have placed him in the grave, nor when you have carried him.

key_terms.اغْتَسِلْ: Perform ghusl; an instruction to undertake ritual bathing
key_terms.الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, a specified occasion for ghusl
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: Eid al-Fiṭr, a specified occasion for ghusl
key_terms.الْقَبْرَ: The grave, in the context of placing the deceased into it
key_terms.حَمَلْتَهُ: You carried him, which is stated here not to require ghusl
key_terms.غَسَّلْتَ مَيِّتًا: You washed a deceased person; an occasion that entails ghusl
key_terms.مَسِّهِ: Touching him, referring to contact with the deceased
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْأَضْحَى: The day of Eid al-Aḍḥā, a specified occasion for ghusl

ai.seo_question: When is ghusl required or recommended according to this hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal guidance on occasions for ghusl, including the days of al-Aḍḥā, al-Fiṭr, Friday, and after washing a deceased person. It also clarifies that merely placing the deceased in the grave or carrying him does not require ghusl due to touch.
